title: 「What makes...」表達成因、關鍵因素與定義
titleZh: 「What makes...」表達成因、關鍵因素與定義

source.file: Sentence Structure 188 -「What makes...」表達成因、關鍵因素與定義.pdf
omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.

formula: What makes + person / thing + adjective / base verb / noun complement + is + key factor

formulas.formula: What makes + person / thing + adjective / base verb / noun complement + is + key factor
What makes + person / thing + adjective / base verb / noun complement?

example: What makes a leader effective is not power, but good judgement.
exampleZh: 令一位領導者有效的，不是權力，而是良好的判斷力。

examples.en: What makes a leader effective is not power, but good judgement.
examples.zh: 令一位領導者有效的，不是權力，而是良好的判斷力。
examples.highlight: What makes a leader effective is not power, but good judgement.

meaning.zh: 本課練習目標句型：What makes + person / thing + adjective / base verb / noun complement + is + key factor。

rules.zh: 在受詞後可以直接使用形容詞，不需要加入 to be。
rules.en: Use an adjective directly after the object What makes + object + adjective ● What makes the room comfortable? ● What makes the lesson interesting? Do not add to be. ● Incorrect: What makes the room to be comfortable? ● Correct: What makes the room comfortable?
examples: Use an adjective directly after the object
What makes + object + adjective
What makes the room comfortable?
What makes the lesson interesting?
Do not add to be.
Incorrect: What makes the room to be comfortable?
Correct: What makes the room comfortable?

rules.zh: 在 makes + 受詞 後使用原形動詞，不使用 to。
rules.en: Use the base verb without “to” What makes + object + base verb ● What makes people laugh? ● What makes the machine stop? Do not use to + verb. ● Incorrect: What makes people to laugh? ● Correct: What makes people laugh?
examples: Use the base verb without “to”
What makes + object + base verb
What makes people laugh?
What makes the machine stop?
Do not use to + verb.
Incorrect: What makes people to laugh?
Correct: What makes people laugh?

rules.zh: 名詞亦可以用來說明某人或某事物成為甚麼。
rules.en: A noun complement may also be used What makes + object + noun complement ● What makes her a good teacher? ● What makes this building a landmark?
examples: A noun complement may also be used
What makes + object + noun complement
What makes her a good teacher?
What makes this building a landmark?

rules.zh: 在本課的陳述句中，整個 What makes... 部分視為一個整體，因此使用 is。
rules.en: Use “is” after the complete What-clause ● What makes the room special is its natural light. ● What makes the programme successful is its simple design.
examples: Use “is” after the complete What-clause
What makes the room special is its natural light.
What makes the programme successful is its simple design.

rules.zh: 在這類問句中，what 本身是主語，因此不需要使用 do 或 does。
rules.en: Do not add “do” or “does” in questions ● Incorrect: What does make this place special? ● Correct: What makes this place special?
examples: Do not add “do” or “does” in questions
Incorrect: What does make this place special?
Correct: What makes this place special?

rules.zh: （這個環境為甚麼良好？） （良好的環境應具備甚麼條件？）
rules.en: Notice the difference between these two questions What makes the environment good? This asks why one particular environment is good. What makes a good environment? This asks what qualities generally define a good environment.
examples: Notice the difference between these two questions
What makes the environment good?
This asks why one particular environment is good.
What makes a good environment?
This asks what qualities generally define a good environment.

rules.zh: 本練習集中訓練現在式 What makes...，不包括過去式 What made...。
rules.en: Present-tense focus This worksheet focuses on What makes... in the present tense. The past-tense form What made... is not included in this exercise.
examples: This worksheet focuses on What makes... in the present tense. The past-tense form What
made... is not included in this exercise.

benefits.zh: 這個句型能清楚指出，究竟是哪一項因素帶來某個結果。 讀者可以立即知道，令房間舒適的關鍵因素是自然光。
benefits.en: It clearly identifies the key cause This structure tells the listener or reader exactly which factor produces a result. ● What makes the room comfortable is the natural light.

benefits.zh: 關鍵答案通常放在 is 後面，因此能得到更明顯的強調。 句子的焦點並非只是「計劃成功」，而是成功背後的「周詳準備」。
benefits.en: It places emphasis on the most important factor The key answer normally appears after is, so it receives more attention. ● What makes the plan successful is careful preparation.

benefits.zh: not A, but B 能先否定一個常見想法，再指出真正原因。
benefits.en: It helps you make clear comparisons The pattern not A, but B allows you to correct a common misunderstanding and highlight the real reason. ● What makes customers stay loyal is not low prices, but good service.

benefits.zh: 與其反覆使用 because，你可以使用 What makes... is...，把原因放在句子的焦點位置。
benefits.en: It gives you an alternative to repeated “because” sentences Compare: ● People trust this service because the staff reply quickly. ● What makes people trust this service is that the staff reply quickly. The second sentence focuses more strongly on the reason.

benefits.zh: 這個句型可以成為現成的表達框架，幫助你分析人物、服務、機構、產品、政策或社會議題。
benefits.en: It provides a useful speaking and writing frame You can use the structure when analysing people, services, organisations, products, policies or social issues. ● What makes a good leader? ● What makes this policy effective? ● What makes people trust an organisation?
